title: Platonic geodesic trees in the $K-$Space
summary: In this paper, We prove that: (A) If $m\ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges (geodesic segments), which form $m$ platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ and $(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m)$ platonic angles with measure $90^{o}.$ (Existence of a Fermat Coordinate system) (B) If $m=2,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree with three vertices and 2 edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ or $150^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$ (Minimal spanning geodesic tree).
